N26.basis: Existing current-objective architecture comparison harness, three comparison runs and six focused tests recorded26Nov; architecture selection and acceptance still incomplete.

rows.deliverable: Inventory all allocation entry points: template, manual, autofill, intelligent generator, balancing, extra duty, superadmin, exchange, restore, import, review, publish, and export. Separate historical records from prospective allocation.
rows.acceptance: Path-to-validator/context/permission map, dated source references, existing behavior and extension points recorded; no duplicate engine proposed.

rows.deliverable: Establish a reproducible current baseline using anonymized real-shaped months, existing suites, and saved proposals; record exact revision, configuration, hardware, and working-tree scope.
rows.acceptance: Coverage, conflicts, fairness, correction count, runtime stages and current failures captured; historical test counts clearly distinguished from fresh results.

rows.deliverable: Build the requirement/constraint register and explicit precedence matrix from current contracts and approved policies. Cover mixed-level pools, effective dates, override boundaries, and imported history.
rows.acceptance: Each constraint has authority, inputs, severity, permitted exception, checker, and test; contradictory older documents are identified rather than silently applied.

rows.deliverable: Define one immutable, versioned scheduling snapshot and invalidation contract covering OT demand, leave, postings, groups, dates, rules, locks, and model preference versions.
rows.acceptance: Editing each relevant input makes affected proposals stale; semantically unchanged input remains reproducible; snapshots exclude unnecessary sensitive notes.

rows.deliverable: Specify measurable objective order and fairness denominators, preserving existing contracts unless amended. Separate required coverage, OT protection, repair stability, call-level equality, burden, and preferences.
rows.acceptance: Worked examples show every trade-off, pooled-level treatment, pro-rata share, rounding and zero-capacity behavior; no silent preference promotion.

rows.deliverable: Ratify acceptance metrics and benchmark corpus before tuning. Include real administrator corrections and critical-duties coverage, not just aggregate score.
rows.acceptance: Fixed scenarios, expected outcomes, regression tolerances, time budgets and sign-off owner recorded; safety failures cannot be averaged away.

rows.deliverable: Define OT demand records: unit, area, weekday, effective dates, time band, required call/skill pool, minimum/target, and provenance. Reuse existing registries.
rows.acceptance: Sundayâ€“Saturday examples cover different units and areas; invalid ranges, negative counts, and incompatible references are rejected.

rows.deliverable: Specify recurring schedule/date-exception precedence, including holidays, OT closure, emergency additional lists, and monthly overrides.
rows.acceptance: A weekly rule plus closure, special opening, and holiday produces one explainable effective requirement per interval; missing configuration is visibly unknown, not assumed zero.

rows.deliverable: Add additive, indexed, versioned OT-demand persistence and conflict-safe administration APIs with actor/time/change history.
rows.acceptance: Isolated migration forward/backward/forward preserves sentinel records; overlapping definitions and concurrent edits receive explicit resolutions; role checks enforced.

rows.deliverable: Build a dedicated admin OT calendar with unit Ã— weekday Ã— call views, area/time detail, copying, date exceptions, preview, and confirmed save.
rows.acceptance: Thursday Unit 4 workload can be entered and traced; keyboard/mobile/error recovery work; copy previews prevent silent overwrites; existing navigation is preserved.

rows.deliverable: Compute available people by actual dated posting, call/group membership, approved leave, overlaps, post-duty rest, and partial-day intervals.
rows.acceptance: Promotion, midmonth transfer, cross-month rest and simultaneous leave/rest each give correct identity-level availability without double subtraction.

rows.deliverable: Match available people to simultaneous OT requirements, respecting pooled levels, area skills and permitted sharing; reconcile existing reserve minima explicitly.
rows.acceptance: A pooled senior counted in two overlapping requirements produces shortage rather than phantom coverage; non-overlapping work can share only where policy permits.

rows.deliverable: Show monthly unit capacity/pressure heatmaps with posted, unavailable, OT-required, reserved and duty-eligible counts and drill-down reasons.
rows.acceptance: Every displayed count reconciles to distinct people and intervals; unknown demand and pending-leave assumptions are visible; restricted details stay restricted.

rows.deliverable: Integrate effective OT demand into template unit eligibility/scoring and every normal prospective assignment validator; enumerate exception behavior separately.
rows.acceptance: An allocation that would consume a mandatory OT reservation is rejected or left unresolved; manual, CPU/GPU, exchange and balancing paths cannot bypass it.

rows.deliverable: Add reviewed monthly OT-calendar import/export using existing unit/call mappings, dry-run validation, source traceability and idempotency.
rows.acceptance: Round-trip, duplicate upload, ambiguous unit, bad weekday and changed mapping scenarios behave predictably; imports never silently activate invalid demand.

rows.deliverable: Add the requested Thursday Unit 4 scenario and variants: heavier elective workload reduces that day's duty contribution when feasible, with fair feasible compensation later.
rows.acceptance: Fixed fixture contrasts demand off/on; Thursday OT capacity remains protected, unchanged days are explained, and infeasible compensation is reported honestly.

rows.deliverable: Exercise OT scarcity and temporal edge cases: all units busy, no eligible senior, overlapping areas, staffing above roster, closure, leap day, partial shift and month boundary.
rows.acceptance: Expected shortages and safe alternatives are asserted; no forced template is mislabeled safe, and no minimum is silently reduced.

rows.deliverable: Inventory canonical leave flows and define profile accounting: dates, intervals, statuses, types, source, actual leave taken versus requests and approved future leave.
rows.acceptance: Existing tables/profile listing are reused; clear counting examples distinguish elapsed approved absence, future approval, pending, cancellation and rejection.

rows.deliverable: Add or expose attributable leave lifecycle history, preserving original import reference, amendments, approval/cancellation actor and reason without a parallel source of truth.
rows.acceptance: Create/edit/approve/cancel can be reconstructed; imported and manually corrected records retain provenance; no destructive overwrite of history.

rows.deliverable: Centralize leave status and interval calculations across calendars, profiles, OT capacity, candidates, safety and reports. Keep pending-leave risk separate from approved blocking.
rows.acceptance: Shared fixtures reconcile every consumer; overlapping duplicate records do not multiply absence; AM/PM/NIGHT combinations follow approved accounting.

rows.deliverable: Extend the existing member profile with searchable leave timeline, filters, linked source/history and authorized create/amend/approve/cancel actions.
rows.acceptance: User edits the canonical record and sees consistent global/profile results; permissions, stale edits and partial-load recovery are tested; private notes are not exposed.

rows.deliverable: Add person/month/year leave statistics with status/type breakdown, calendar-day versus working-day definitions and cross-month clipping.
rows.acceptance: Numbers reconcile to source intervals; overlapping periods, midnight boundaries, transfers and leap years are covered; unavailable historical coverage is disclosed.

rows.deliverable: Report leave taken separately from entitlement balances; add balance fields only if a specific policy amendment is approved.
rows.acceptance: No balance, carry-forward or deduction is invented; the UI states counting basis and data coverage; leave volume is never used as a disciplinary score.

rows.deliverable: Connect leave changes to affected-duty/OT impact previews and scoped repair proposals, including concurrent approval versus allocation.
rows.acceptance: Leave approval never silently reassigns duties; pending previews invalidate appropriately; impacted locks/published months surface for authorized resolution.

rows.deliverable: Validate leave reconciliation and import/profile lifecycle end to end, including alias merges, duplicate imports, amended dates, cancellation and access control.
rows.acceptance: Before/after counts agree across profile, calendar, OT capacity and allocation; archived history remains attributable; repeat import/application is idempotent.

rows.deliverable: Benchmark joint unit/person CP-SAT against an iterative template-person feasibility/repair loop using the same constraints and scenarios. Select and document the architecture.
rows.acceptance: Compare safe coverage, unit/person fairness, runtime, memory and maintainability; include a case where the sequential template prevents an otherwise feasible rota.

rows.deliverable: Implement the selected month-wide unit-allocation approach behind a feature flag, preserving original duty requirements, explicit scope and approved objective precedence.
rows.acceptance: Cross-day unit choices respond to later scarcity; no lost/duplicated required slots; legacy reviewed generation remains available for rollback.

rows.deliverable: Couple person allocation with OT reservations and call/skill feasibility, including simultaneous pools and next-day rest induced by new duties.
rows.acceptance: A duty that removes the only eligible next-day OT member is prevented; combined final schedule passes independent interval and staffing checks.

rows.deliverable: Preserve exact locked duties, explicit repair scope, existing commitments and published-month protection across the new planning path.
rows.acceptance: Repair cannot widen scope silently; locked unfilled duties remain visible; both preserved and proposed assignments are validated together.

rows.deliverable: Balance monthly call-level load, weekends, nights, holidays, unit contributions and history against compatible opportunities; expose unavoidable differences.
rows.acceptance: Zero availability, small pools and unequal unit size produce explainable targets; OT protection does not silently overturn approved per-person fairness.

rows.deliverable: Produce bounded, distinct feasible alternatives with before/after comparisons and no regression of approved higher-priority objectives.
rows.acceptance: Alternatives are distinct by actual allocation, preserve coverage/locks, and show marginal OT/fairness/preferences trade-offs; absence of alternatives is explicit.

rows.deliverable: Add actionable infeasibility/shortage explanations and solver evidence: rejected eligibility, conflicting requirements, bound/status and unproven objectives.
rows.acceptance: Distinguish input-data gap, no feasible full coverage, timeout and proven optimum; explanations reference actual constraints and avoid claiming a minimal conflict without proof.

rows.deliverable: Add reviewed emergency repair for unexpected leave, OT surge or closure with bounded change count, safe alternatives and attributable undo/conflict checks.
rows.acceptance: Emergency scenario minimizes changes under approved priorities; no published modification or automatic apply; undo refuses intervening conflicting edits.

rows.deliverable: Add robustness scenarios for plausible pending approvals, sudden senior absence and extra OT demand; report fragility separately from the official plan.
rows.acceptance: Stress runs do not alter live input or silently reserve hypothetical absences; they quantify shortages, affected duties and feasible contingency choices.

rows.deliverable: Validate solver/checker correctness with small-instance exhaustive oracles, randomized/property tests, metamorphic cases and hard departmental fixtures.
rows.acceptance: Independent oracle catches invalid/less-covered results on bounded cases; renaming/order changes cannot change feasibility; added optional capacity cannot reduce theoretical feasibility.

rows.deliverable: Profile member, template and optimizer stages separately: database/context, candidate generation, HTTP, startup, encoding, kernel, readback, CP-SAT and validation.
rows.acceptance: Representative cold/warm runs with hardware/browser/config metadata identify real bottlenecks; timings distinguish work moved to GPU from CPU search.

rows.deliverable: Design GPU batching only for independent numeric evaluations or search hints; keep dependent staffing/fairness state synchronized and authoritative.
rows.acceptance: Architecture explains when scores become stale; parallel evaluation never independently commits competing allocations; benchmark identifies a worthwhile workload.

rows.deliverable: Optimize measured GPU overhead through bounded worker/buffer reuse, batched transfers, fewer request exchanges and workload-size crossover rules where beneficial.
rows.acceptance: Before/after end-to-end evidence includes memory and cold start; retain or ship each optimization only if evidence supports it, recording rejected experiments.

rows.deliverable: Extend exact integer and deterministic tie parity across new kernels, batches, boundary sizes and hardware; keep canonical server validation.
rows.acceptance: CPU/GPU rows and rankings agree; malformed, overflow, stale or forged outputs fail safely; distinguish harmless seed differences from final feasibility/equivalence checks.

rows.deliverable: Preserve Automatic's existing 20% whole-workflow advantage gate with current workload/config/adapter fingerprints and expiry; expose honest compute attribution.
rows.acceptance: Slow/unsupported/stale hardware selects server; a valid faster workload selects GPU; UI identifies GPU ranking/hints separately from CPU optimization.

rows.deliverable: Extend GPU failure/recovery and browser matrix testing: loss, crash, timeout, blocked API, memory limits, changed adapter and interrupted network.
rows.acceptance: Bounded recovery reaches a reviewed server draft or explicit resumable failure; no duplicate operation/apply, silent background work or unsafe browser flags.

rows.deliverable: Establish a versioned local-model evaluation set: departmental language, ambiguous adjustments, pooled calls, numerical limits, OT pressure and leave explanations.
rows.acceptance: Score typed intent accuracy, unsupported claims, abstention, latency and RAM/VRAM; compare current Qwen baseline before selecting another model.

rows.deliverable: Prototype optional proposer/critic or specialist-model routing against a single-model baseline, with strict schema, deadlines, resource admission and abstention.
rows.acceptance: Demonstrates improvement on unseen cases worth its latency/memory; disagreement goes to review; no majority vote overrides a validator; unnecessary ensemble is not shipped.

rows.deliverable: Ground assistant output in authorized current rules, OT demand and approved teaching evidence; cite source/version and reject unsupported numerical or policy changes.
rows.acceptance: Prompt-injection, stale-context and invented-fact cases fail safely; minimized inputs omit leave reasons/profile comments; unapproved cloud endpoints are never used.

rows.deliverable: Design deterministic incident/recovery orchestration with optional AI explanation: stage-specific errors, durable revisions, idempotent retries, circuit breakers and manual resume.
rows.acceptance: Model unavailable/wrong/malformed during an interrupted operation cannot cause repair, policy changes or replayed writes; recovery outcome is observable and attributable.

rows.deliverable: Expand approved-example learning with month-separated holdouts, exception exclusion, duplicate suppression, versioned evaluation, activation and rollback; gate any fine-tuning proposal separately.
rows.acceptance: Demonstrate correction reduction without safety/coverage/fairness regression on unseen departmental cases; rejected examples cannot remain active training evidence.

rows.deliverable: Run end-to-end regression on imports, profiles, leave, OT setup, all allocation paths, review, publish, Excel/report export, and existing exception ledgers.
rows.acceptance: Isolated workflow evidence and responsive/accessibility checks; exports reconcile with saved assignments and shortages; unrelated current work remains intact.

rows.deliverable: Stress concurrency, migration and security boundaries with real disposable PostgreSQL: simultaneous approvals/applies/edits, stale snapshots, role changes and bounded hostile inputs.
rows.acceptance: Atomicity, lock ordering, idempotency and rollback hold; unknown commit outcomes resolve by durable read; no permission escalation or leaking private leave data.

rows.deliverable: Rehearse outages and disaster recovery: backend restart, connection drop during apply, failed migration, restored backup, assistant outage and GPU failure.
rows.acceptance: Restore into an isolated environment and reconcile records/audit history; agreed recovery objectives and runbook recorded; no operational fault injection.

rows.deliverable: Conduct shadow/reviewed departmental pilots over several contrasting months, document outcomes, release notes, training, monitoring, feature-flag rollback and final approval.
rows.acceptance: Ratified targets met with zero new unauthorized hard-rule violations; correction count and OT protection demonstrably improve; user signs off before production rollout and tracker closure.

next_dependency: Finish current-source system proof and N02/N05/N06 evidence before selecting architecture/N27. No queued downstream item is silently marked complete.
